1.word_for_word: ekatriṃśe — in the thirty-first chapter; nirāśāḥ tāḥ — those gopīs, despairing; punaḥ pulinam āgatāḥ — returned to the riverbank; kṛṣṇam eva anugāyantyaḥ — singing only of Kṛṣṇa; prārthayante tad-āgamam — pray for his return; he dayita — O beloved; te janmanā vrajaḥ adhikam jayati — by your birth Vraja flourishes beyond all places; indirā lakṣmīḥ atra hi śrayate — Lakṣmī herself now dwells here; tāvakāḥ tvadīyā gopī-janāḥ — your own gopīs; tvayi tvad-artham eva kathañcit dhṛtāsavaḥ — somehow maintaining their lives solely for you; tvām vicinvate — search for you; tvayā dṛśyatām — therefore become visible to them; asmābhiḥ bhavān dṛśyatām — or: let us behold you; ete vicinvate iti tvayā dṛśyatām — or: look upon us and see how we search
1.translation: In the thirty-first chapter, the despairing gopīs return to the Yamunā bank and, singing only of Kṛṣṇa, pray for his return. ‘O beloved, by your birth Vraja has become supremely glorious, for Lakṣmī herself now resides here. Yet your own gopīs somehow keep their lives only for your sake while searching everywhere for you. Therefore show yourself to us.’ Śrīdhara allows several nuances of the final expression: ‘be seen by us,’ or ‘look upon us—see how we search for you.’

2.word_for_word: śarad-udāśaye — in a lake during autumn; sādhu jātam sarasijam — a perfectly blossomed lotus; tasya udare yā śrīḥ — the beauty in its center; tām muṣṇāti harati yā dṛk — the glance that steals even that beauty; he surata-nātha — O lord of amorous union; varada — O giver of boons; aśulka-dāsikāḥ — maidservants who ask no wages; no nighnataḥ — while you kill us; śastreṇa eva vadhaḥ vadhaḥ kim dṛśā vadhaḥ na bhavati — is killing only by a weapon called killing; does killing by a glance not count; tvad-dṛśā apahṛta-prāṇa-pratyarpaṇāya — to restore the life stolen by your glance; tvayā dṛśyatām — let yourself be seen
2.translation: One gopī continues: ‘Your glance steals the beauty from the very heart of a perfectly blossomed autumn lotus. O lord of love, O giver of boons, we are your unpaid maidservants. If you kill us with that glance, is it not killing merely because no weapon is used? Restore the lives your glance has taken by showing yourself to us.’ Śrīdhara says that the refrain ‘let yourself be seen’ may be supplied throughout the song where appropriate.

3.word_for_word: bahubhyaḥ mṛtyubhyaḥ kṛpayā rakṣitvā — after mercifully saving us from many deaths; kim iti idānīm dṛśā manmatham preṣya ghātayasi — why now send Cupid through your glance to kill us; viṣa-mayāt jalāt apyayaḥ — destruction from poisonous water; vyāla-rākṣasāt aghāsurāt — from the serpent-demon Aghāsura; varṣāt mārutāt vaidyuta-analāt — from rain, wind and lightning-fire; aśani-pātāt — from thunderbolts; vṛṣaḥ ariṣṭaḥ — the bull Ariṣṭa; mayātmajāt vyomāt — from Vyoma, son of Maya; viśvataḥ anyasmāt api bhayāt — from every other danger; kāliya-damanādinā rakṣitāḥ — protected by your subduing Kāliya and other deeds; kim idānīm upekṣase — why abandon us now; editor note — Ariṣṭa and Vyoma are spoken of as past either because their future deaths were known from Garga and others or because the narration of separation telescopes them into remembered dangers
3.translation: ‘You have mercifully protected us from death again and again—from poisonous water, Aghāsura, violent rain and wind, lightning and thunderbolts, from the bull Ariṣṭa, Vyomāsura and every kind of danger, including Kāliya's poison. Why save us from all these deaths only to send Cupid through your glance to kill us now? Why abandon us?’ The source notes that Ariṣṭa and Vyoma, whose deaths occur later in the narrative sequence, may be spoken of as past because they were already known through prophetic statements such as Garga's, or because the language of separation gathers the whole pattern of Kṛṣṇa's protection into a single remembered experience.

4.word_for_word: viśva-pālanāya avatīrṇasya — of you who descended to protect the universe; bhakta-upekṣā atyantam anucitā — neglect of devotees is utterly unfitting; na khalu yaśodā-sutaḥ — surely you are not merely Yaśodā's son; sarva-prāṇinām buddhi-sākṣī — witness of the minds of all living beings; nanu sa kim dṛśyaḥ bhavati — objection: how can that transcendent witness be visible; vikhanasā brahmaṇā — by Brahmā; viśva-pālanāya prārthitaḥ — requested to protect the universe; sātvatām kule udeyivān — you arose in the clan of the Sātvatas
4.translation: ‘For one who has descended to protect the universe, neglecting his own devotees is utterly improper. Friend, you cannot be merely the son of Yaśodā; you are the witness within the intelligence of every living being.’ If one asks how such an inner witness can become visible, the answer is that Brahmā petitioned him to protect the universe and he therefore manifested visibly in the clan of the Sātvatas.

5.word_for_word: etad prārthanā-catuṣṭayam sampādaya — fulfill these four petitions of us, your devotees; he vṛṣṇi-dhurya — O foremost of the Vṛṣṇis; saṃsṛteḥ bhayāt — from the fear of saṃsāra; te caraṇam īyuṣām — for beings who approach your feet for refuge; viracitam dattam abhayam yena — your hand grants fearlessness; he kānta — O beloved; kāmadam varadam — granting desired boons; śriyaḥ karam gṛhṇāti — the hand that takes Lakṣmī's hand; tat bhavat-kara-saroruham — that lotus hand of yours; naḥ śirasi dehi — place it upon our heads
5.translation: The gopīs now formulate a series of four requests: ‘O foremost of the Vṛṣṇis, the hand by which you grant fearlessness to those who seek your feet as refuge from saṃsāra—the same boon-giving hand that holds Śrī's hand—place that lotus hand upon our heads.’

6.word_for_word: he vraja-jana-ārti-han — O destroyer of the suffering of Vraja's people; he vīra — O hero; nija-janānām smayaḥ garvaḥ — the pride of your own people; tasya dhvaṃsanam smitam — your smile destroys it; he sakhe — O friend; bhavat-kiṅkarīḥ naḥ bhaja āśraya — accept us, your maidservants; sm iti niścitam — ‘indeed,’ with certainty; jala-ruha-ānanam — lotus face; cāru — beautiful; naḥ darśaya — show it to us
6.translation: ‘O destroyer of Vraja's distress, O hero, your smile destroys even the pride of your own beloved people. Friend, accept us who are your maidservants. First of all, show us your beautiful lotus face.’

7.word_for_word: praṇatānām dehinām pāpa-karśanam — destroying the sins of embodied beings who bow down; tṛṇa-carān paśūn api anugacchati kṛpayā — out of compassion it follows even the grass-eating cows; śriyaḥ niketanam — abode of Śrī; phaṇinaḥ phaṇāsu arpitam — placed upon the hoods of the serpent Kāliya; te pada-ambujam — your lotus foot; naḥ kuceṣu kṛṇu kuru — place it upon our breasts; hṛc-chayam kāmam kṛndhi chindhi — cut away the desire lodged in our hearts
7.translation: ‘Your lotus foot destroys the sins of all embodied beings who bow to it; out of compassion it follows even the grass-eating cows. It is the abode of Śrī and, through your heroic power, was placed upon Kāliya's hoods. Put that lotus foot upon our breasts and cut away the desire burning in our hearts.’

8.word_for_word: he puṣkara-īkṣaṇa — O lotus-eyed one; tava madhurayā girā — by your sweet voice; valgūni vākyāni — charming words; budhānām manojñayā — pleasing even to the wise; hṛdyayā gambhīrayā — heartfelt and deep; muhyatīḥ imāḥ naḥ — us who are fainting in bewilderment; vidhi-karīḥ kiṅkarīḥ — maidservants who carry out your commands; adhara-sīdhunā — with the nectar/wine of your lips; āpyāyayasva saṃjīvaya — revive and nourish us
8.translation: ‘O lotus-eyed one, your sweet voice speaks charming words, profound and heart-pleasing even to the wise. We, your obedient maidservants, are now fainting. Revive us with the intoxicating nectar of your lips.’

9.word_for_word: asmākam tvad-virahe maraṇam prāptam eva — separation from you had already brought us to death; tvat-kathā-amṛtam pāyayadbhiḥ sukṛtibhiḥ vañcitam — but virtuous people who make us drink the nectar of your stories cheated death of us; kathā eva amṛtam — the narrative itself is nectar; tapta-jīvanam — life for those scorched by suffering; kavibhiḥ brahmavidbhiḥ api īḍitam — praised even by sages and knowers of Brahman; deva-bhogyam amṛtam taiḥ tucchīkṛtam — compared with it, the gods' nectar is made insignificant; kalmaṣa-apaham — removing impurity; kāma-karma-nirasanam — destroying desire and karmic action; śravaṇa-maṅgalam — auspicious merely through hearing; śrīmat — possessed of beauty/fortune; suśāntam — deeply pacifying; deva-amṛtam tu mādakam — ordinary divine nectar intoxicates instead; ye bhuvi gṛṇanti — those who spread it on earth; te bhūridāḥ — they are great givers; jīvitam dadati — they give life; alternative: pūrva-janmasu bahu dattavantaḥ sukṛtinaḥ — or ‘bhūridāḥ’ means people made virtuous by great generosity in former lives; kevalam kathāmṛtam gṛṇanti api atidhanyāḥ — even those who only proclaim the stories are extraordinarily blessed; kim punaḥ ye tvām paśyanti — how much more those who see you
9.translation: ‘Death had already reached us in separation from you, but the blessed souls who made us drink the nectar of your stories prevented it. Your stories are themselves nectar because they give life to those scorched by suffering. Sages and knowers of Brahman praise them, rendering even the gods' nectar insignificant. Your kathā removes impurity and the bondage of desire and action; it is auspicious merely to hear, beautiful and profoundly peaceful, whereas ordinary nectar merely intoxicates. Those who spread this nectar across the earth are the greatest givers, because they give life itself.’ Alternatively, ‘great givers’ may mean souls whose great generosity in former births has made them worthy to distribute such nectar. If even those who speak only of Kṛṣṇa are so blessed, how much more blessed are those who behold him directly—hence the gopīs again pray that he show himself.

10.word_for_word: mat-kathā-śravaṇena eva nirvṛtā bhavata — imagined reply: be satisfied simply by hearing my stories; kim mad-darśanena — what need have you to see me; na — the gopīs reject this; tvad-vilāsa-kṣubhita-cittāḥ vayam — our minds have been agitated by your playful gestures; tatra api śāntim na vindāmaḥ — even hearing does not bring peace now; prahasitām iti — the verse begins ‘your bright laughter’; he priya — O beloved; kuhaka — O deceiver; kapaṭa — trickster; saṃvidaḥ — secret understandings; saṅketa-narmāṇi — private signals and jokes
10.translation: If Kṛṣṇa were to answer, ‘Be satisfied merely by hearing my stories—why must you see me?’ the gopīs reply that his own playful behavior has agitated their minds too deeply for hearing alone now to pacify them. ‘O beloved deceiver, your bright laughter, your secret understandings, signs and intimate jokes have disturbed us beyond repose.’

11.word_for_word: tvayi vayam ati-prema-ārdra-cittāḥ — our hearts are softened by overwhelming love for you; tvam punaḥ asmāsu kena hetunā kapaṭam ācarasi — why then do you act deceitfully toward us; he nātha he kānta — O Lord, O beloved; yadā vrajāt calasi paśūn cārayan — when you leave Vraja to herd the animals; tat nalina-sundaram komalam te padam — your soft foot, beautiful as a lotus; śilaiḥ kaṇiśaiḥ tṛṇaiḥ aṅkuraiḥ ca sīdati — may suffer from stones, sharp grain-stalks, grasses and shoots; naḥ manaḥ kalilatām asvāsthyam gacchati — our minds become troubled and unhealthy; tvad-duḥkha-śaṅkita-cittāḥ — our hearts fear pain for you
11.translation: ‘Our hearts are utterly softened by love for you; why then are you deceitful toward us? O Lord, O beloved, whenever you leave Vraja to herd the cows, we fear that your soft lotus-like feet may be hurt by stones, sharp stalks, grass and shoots. Merely imagining your pain throws our minds into distress.’

12.word_for_word: dina-parikṣaye sāyaṃ-kāle — at the end of the day, in the evening; nīla-kuntalaiḥ āvṛtam — covered by dark locks; ghana-rajasvalam go-rajaḥ-churitam — thickly dusted with the dust raised by the cows; vanaruha-ānanam — lotus-like face; ali-mālā-ākula-parāga-churita-padma-tulyam — like a lotus powdered with pollen and surrounded by bees; muhur muhuḥ darśayan — repeatedly showing it to us; naḥ manasi kevalam smaram yacchasi — you merely place love-longing in our minds; na tu saṅgam dadāsi — but do not grant union; smaram — that which agitates even by mere remembrance
12.translation: ‘Then at day's end you return with your dark locks falling around your face, your lotus countenance thickly covered by the dust of the cows—like a pollen-covered lotus ringed by bees. Again and again you let us see that face, only to plant ever stronger longing in our minds, yet you do not grant us union. This is your deception.’ ‘Smara’ is so called because even remembrance of him causes agitation.

13.word_for_word: adhunā kapaṭam vihāya — now abandon this deception; he adhi-han — O destroyer of distress; he ramaṇa — O lover; padmajena brahmaṇā arcitam — worshiped by lotus-born Brahmā; āpadi dhyeyam — to be meditated upon in danger; dhyāna-mātreṇa āpat-nivartakam — dispelling calamity merely by meditation; śantamam — most soothing; sevā-samaye api sukhatamam — supremely delightful even while being served; te caraṇa-paṅkajam — your lotus foot; kāma-tāpa-śāntaye — to pacify the burning of desire; naḥ staneṣu arpaya — place it upon our breasts
13.translation: ‘Enough deception now. O destroyer of distress, O beloved, place upon our breasts your lotus foot, worshiped by lotus-born Brahmā, which one need only meditate upon in danger for calamity to disappear. That foot is supremely soothing and blissful even in the act of serving it; place it upon us and pacify the fire of longing.’

14.word_for_word: he vīra — O hero; te adhara-amṛtam no vitara dehi — give us the nectar of your lips; svaritena nāditena veṇunā suṣṭhu cumbitam — deeply kissed by your sounding flute; nāda-amṛta-vāsitam — perfumed by the nectar of its music; itara-rāga-vismāraṇam — causing all other attachments to be forgotten; nṛṇām itareṣu sārvabhauma-ādi-sukheṣu rāgam icchām vismārayati — making people forget desire even for imperial and other worldly pleasures
14.translation: ‘O hero, give us the nectar of your lips, lips thoroughly kissed by your resonant flute and perfumed by the nectar of its sound. That nectar makes a person forget every other attachment, even desire for the greatest worldly pleasures such as universal sovereignty.’

15.word_for_word: kṣaṇam api tvad-adarśane duḥkham — even a moment without seeing you is painful; darśane ca sukham — seeing you is bliss; sarva-saṅga-parityāgena yatayaḥ iva vayam — we have abandoned all other attachments like renunciants; truṭiḥ kṣaṇārdham api yugavat bhavati — even half a moment becomes like an age; dina-ante te śrīmat mukham īkṣamāṇānām — when at day's end we finally behold your beautiful face; dṛśām pakṣma-kṛt brahmā — Brahmā, maker of eyelids for our eyes; jaḍaḥ mandaḥ eva — must be dull and foolish; nimeṣa-mātram api antaram asahyam — even the interruption of a blink is unbearable
15.translation: ‘Even an instant without seeing you is misery, whereas seeing you is bliss. Having abandoned all other attachments like renunciants, we experience even half a moment of separation as an age. And when at last we behold your beautiful face at day's end, Brahmā, who created eyelids that interrupt our vision by blinking, seems dull and foolish to us. Even that fraction of separation is unbearable.’

16.word_for_word: he acyuta — O Acyuta; patīn sutān anvayān tat-sambandhinaḥ bhrātṝn bāndhavān ca atilaṅghya — leaving behind husbands, sons, family relations, brothers and kinsmen; tava samīpam āgatā vayam — we came to you; gati-vidaḥ — you who know our movements/coming, or know the modes of song; gati-vidaḥ vayam vā — alternatively, we know the path to you; tava udgītena uccaiḥ gītena mohitāḥ — enchanted by your loud song; he kitava he śaṭha — O gambler/deceiver, O rogue; evaṃ-bhūtā yoṣitaḥ niśi svayam āgatāḥ — women such as us who came of our own accord at night; tvām ṛte kaḥ tyajet — who besides you would abandon them; na kaḥ api — no one
16.translation: ‘O Acyuta, we crossed beyond husbands, sons, relatives, brothers and all family ties to come to you. You knew very well that we were coming—indeed your own song enchanted and summoned us. O deceiver, O rogue, what man other than you would abandon women who came to him voluntarily in the middle of the night?’ Śrīdhara also notes alternate nuances of ‘gati-vit’: Kṛṣṇa knows their movement, knows musical modes, or the gopīs themselves know only the path leading to him.

17.word_for_word: tvayā tyaktānām asmākam — for us now abandoned by you; prāktana-tvad-darśana-nidāna-hṛd-rogasya — the heart-disease whose cause was our earlier vision of you; tvat-saṅgatyā eva cikitsām kuru — cure it only by renewed contact with you; rahasi iti — beginning ‘in private’; śriyaḥ dhāma te bṛhat viśālam uraḥ — your broad chest, abode of Śrī; vīkṣya — having seen it; atispṛhā bhavati — intense longing arises; muhur muhuḥ manaḥ muhyati — again and again the mind becomes overwhelmed
17.translation: ‘The disease in our hearts was caused by our earlier sight of you; now that you have abandoned us, cure that disease by your presence alone. When we remember your broad chest, the very abode of Śrī, intense longing arises and our minds repeatedly lose their composure.’

18.word_for_word: tava vyaktiḥ abhivyaktiḥ — your manifestation; vraja-vanaukasām sarveṣām aviśeṣeṇa — for all residents of Vraja's forests without distinction; vṛjina-hantrī — destroyer of suffering; viśva-maṅgalam — universally auspicious, embodiment of all blessing; tvat-spṛha-ātmanām — of us whose whole being longs for you; manāk īṣat kim api tyaja muñca — give just a little of that remedy; kārpaṇyam akurvan dehi — do not be miserly; give it; sva-jana-hṛd-rogāṇām — for the heart-disease of your own people; ati-gopyam niṣūdanam nivartakam auṣadham — the deeply secret medicine that destroys it; tat tvam eva vetsi — you alone know what that medicine is
18.translation: ‘Your very manifestation removes the suffering of all who live in Vraja and is auspicious for the whole world. We whose entire beings thirst for you ask only a little—do not be miserly with the remedy. You alone know the deeply secret medicine that can cure the heart-disease of your own people.’ Śrīdhara says the final words conceal an intimate implication: Kṛṣṇa himself knows the remedy they are requesting.

19.word_for_word: ati-prema-dharṣitāḥ rudatyaḥ āhuḥ — overcome by extreme love, they speak while weeping; he priya — O beloved; te sukumāram padābjam — your exceedingly tender lotus foot; kaṭhineṣu kuceṣu sammardana-śaṅkitāḥ — fearing it might be hurt even by our hard breasts; śanaiḥ dadhīmahi — we place it gently; tvam tu tena āṭavīm aṭasi — yet you roam the forest on those feet; ‘nayasi’ iti pāṭhe — variant reading ‘you lead’; paśūn vā kāñcit anyām vā ātmānam eva vā nayasi — you lead the cows, perhaps another beloved, or yourself; kūrpa-ādibhiḥ sūkṣma-pāṣāṇa-ādibhiḥ — by sharp pebbles and small stones; kim svit na vyathate — are those feet not hurt; katham nu nāma na vyathet — how could they possibly not hurt; bhavān eva āyuḥ jīvanam yāsām — for us whose very life is you; naḥ dhīḥ bhramati muhyati — our minds reel; dadhīmahi dhartum yogyam — grammatical note: the form conveys ‘we deem them fit to be held [gently]’; tvayi dhṛtāsavaḥ — this returns to the opening theme that their lives are held only in him
19.translation: Overcome by love and weeping, the gopīs end: ‘Beloved, your lotus feet are so tender that when we place them upon our breasts we do so gently, fearing even our bodies may hurt them. Yet with those same feet you wander the rough forest. Are they not pierced by tiny stones and sharp pebbles? How could they not be hurt? You are our very life, and the thought makes our minds reel.’ A variant reading says ‘you lead,’ allowing the sense that Kṛṣṇa leads the cows, perhaps another companion, or simply himself through the forest. Śrīdhara's grammatical note reinforces the tenderness of ‘we would hold them gently,’ and the closing returns to the song's opening declaration that the gopīs preserve their lives only in Kṛṣṇa.
